module.purpose: Provides the Google Calendar implementation of the application calendar-service contract, translating scheduling operations into Google Calendar API calls, availability queries, cache operations, and webhook-channel lifecycle updates.
module.summary: This module adapts application calendar events and availability requests to Google Calendar. It builds event payloads with attendees, recurrence, conferencing, locations, and rich descriptions; performs create, update, delete, and free/busy operations; caches availability; handles calendar selection and pagination; and manages Google push-notification subscriptions together with persisted selected-calendar records. Authentication and API retry behavior are delegated to the calendar authentication layer.
module.businessContext: Supports scheduling and availability synchronization for users connected to Google Calendar. Failures can prevent event creation, produce incorrect availability, or leave webhook subscriptions and cache state inconsistent.

invariants.description: Google event attendees are emitted with accepted response status.
Created events always return an application event object with an id fallback.
Availability cache keys expand requested bounds to calendar-month boundaries.
Google free/busy requests are chunked so each request covers at most ninety days.
Unwatching deletes cache state and stops channels before repopulating remaining-calendar cache.
Selected-calendar persistence requires a credential userId and otherwise returns without writing.

assumptions.description: Callers provide application event and calendar objects compatible with the imported Calendar types.
Webhook operation expects GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_TOKEN and a usable webhook base URL.
Selected-calendar repository records contain Google channel fields and event-type associations.
Google free/busy requests cannot cover more than ninety days.

concurrencyModel.notes: Methods are asynchronous and rely on Google API and repository operations. Channel stopping uses Promise.allSettled concurrently; availability chunks and cache population are processed sequentially.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A valid calendar service event is created in the selected external calendar.
moduleContractTests.then: Google Calendar receives an events.insert request and the returned value has type "google_calendar" and an event id.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins event payload translation and provider identity.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An existing Google Calendar event is updated with the supplied title, timing, attendees, and location.
moduleContractTests.then: Google Calendar receives an events.update request for uid with the translated event payload.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Guards update semantics and external calendar selection.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Google reports that the event is already deleted or belongs to another calendar.
given: calendar.events.delete rejects with { code: 410 } or { code: 404 }

moduleContractTests.scenario: Selected calendars contain calendars from integrations other than Google Calendar.
moduleContractTests.then: The result is [] and no Google availability request is made.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Availability is requested for a period longer than Google Calendar's 90-day freebusy limit.
given: dateTo is more than 90 days after dateFrom
moduleContractTests.then: Google freebusy requests cover the period in chunks of at most 90 days and the busy results are combined.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A matching cached availability result exists and cache serving is enabled.
moduleContractTests.then: The cached busy intervals are returned without calling Google freebusy.query.

moduleContractTests.scenario: No Google calendars are explicitly selected and primary-calendar fallback is enabled.
moduleContractTests.then: Availability is requested for the valid primary calendar.
The call resolves without creating a Google watch channel.

moduleContractTests.scenario: The selected calendar already has a Google channel for another event type.
given: allCalendarsWithSubscription contains a matching existing channel
moduleContractTests.then: No new events.watch request is made and the existing channel properties are reused.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A calendar remains watched by another event type after one event type is unwatched.
moduleContractTests.then: The selected calendar channel fields are cleared but the Google channel is not stopped.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Prevents disrupting subscriptions still in use.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Availability is fetched for selected Google calendars with known calendar time zones.
given: calendar list entries provide id and timeZone
moduleContractTests.then: Each busy interval includes the time zone associated with its calendar.
